text: Databases are organised systems for storing and managing information. There are two main types: SQL and NoSQL. SQL databases store data in tables, which look like spreadsheets with rows and columns. To get information from them, you write queries using a special language. NoSQL databases are more flexible and are useful for large amounts of unstructured data. Before building a database, you need data modelling to plan how your information connects together. Finally, indexes help the database find data much faster, like an index in a book. Understanding these basics makes working with data much easier.
